A tenancy agreement should be in writing and signed by both the landlord and the tenant. It should state the rent amount, the due date, the length of the tenancy, the security deposit, and who pays for repairs and utilities. Keeping a signed copy helps both sides if a disagreement comes up later.

When a tenant stops paying rent, the landlord should first give written notice of the unpaid amount and a reasonable time to pay. If the rent is still unpaid, the landlord can apply to the rent authority or court for an eviction order. The landlord should not remove the tenant or their belongings by force.

The security deposit is usually returned when the tenancy ends, after deducting only unpaid rent or the cost of damage beyond normal wear and tear. The landlord should explain any deduction in writing. Taking photos of the property when moving in and moving out helps settle deposit disagreements.

Rent can usually be increased only as the tenancy agreement allows, or after giving the tenant proper notice. A sudden increase without notice is a common cause of disputes. Tenants should check their agreement for the agreed increase rate and notice period.

Major repairs to the structure, plumbing and wiring are normally the landlord's job, while small day-to-day upkeep is often the tenant's. The tenancy agreement should say who handles what. Tenants should report problems in writing so there is a record.

column2: Basic Elements of a Valid Contract
column5: A contract is usually valid when there is a clear offer, acceptance of that offer, free consent from both parties, and something of value exchanged. Both parties must be legally able to make the agreement. A written contract is much easier to prove than a spoken one.

A breach happens when one party does not do what the contract requires. The other party can usually claim damages to cover their loss, or ask the court to order the contract to be carried out. Keeping records of messages and payments helps prove the breach.

A contract should state how much must be paid, when it is due and how it will be paid. It can also set a fair penalty for late payment. If a payment is late, the other party should send a written reminder before taking further action.

Many contracts can be ended early by giving the notice period written in the agreement. Ending a contract without following that notice can count as a breach. Both sides should keep a copy of the termination notice.
Signing an agreement shows that a person accepts its terms. Important agreements are often signed in front of witnesses, who also sign. Each party should keep an original signed copy.

If a product is faulty or damaged when it arrives, the buyer can usually ask the seller for a repair, a replacement or a refund. The buyer should report the problem quickly. Keeping the receipt and the original packaging makes the claim much easier.

A warranty is a promise from the seller or maker to fix or replace a product if it fails within a set time. The buyer should read what the warranty covers and keep the warranty card and receipt. Damage caused by misuse is usually not covered.

When an online order arrives late, wrong or damaged, the buyer should contact the seller in writing with photos and the order number. Many online sellers offer a return window, so the buyer should act before it ends. Paying through a method that keeps a record makes disputes easier to settle.

If a seller refuses to solve a problem, the buyer can first send a written notice explaining the issue and what they want. If that fails, a complaint can be filed with the consumer court or the consumer protection authority. The buyer should attach receipts, photos and copies of messages.

Sellers should not advertise false features, hidden charges or a price they will not honour. If a buyer was misled into a purchase, they may be able to cancel the deal and ask for a refund. Screenshots of the advertisement are useful evidence.

A written employment contract should state the job title, salary, working hours, leave and the notice period for leaving. Both the employer and the employee should sign it and keep a copy. Any later change to the terms should also be agreed in writing.

If an employer does not pay salary on time, the employee should first ask for it in writing and keep records such as pay slips, bank statements and messages. If the salary is still not paid, the employee can file a complaint with the labour department or the labour court.

An employee who wants to leave should give written notice as the contract requires. Leaving without serving the notice period may lead to a deduction from the final salary. The employer should clear the final dues once the notice period ends.

An employer should normally give a reason and proper notice, or pay in place of notice, before ending someone's job. A dismissal that does not follow the contract or the rules may be challenged. The employee should ask for the termination letter in writing.

Every workplace should have a way to report harassment, such as an inquiry committee. The person affected should write down what happened, when it happened and who saw it. If the workplace does not act, the complaint can be taken to the relevant ombudsperson.

A marriage should be registered with the local union council so there is an official record. The marriage contract lists details such as the names of both parties, the witnesses and any agreed terms. Both spouses should keep a copy of the registered document.

Ending a marriage usually involves a formal written process and, in many cases, notice to the local council or an application to the family court. The exact steps depend on who starts the process and the law that applies. People should get proper legal advice before taking any step.

When parents separate, the family court decides custody mainly on the basis of the child's welfare. The court may look at the child's age, schooling and which parent can provide a stable home. The parent without custody is usually allowed to meet the child at set times.

A spouse or children who are not being supported can ask the family court for maintenance, which is a regular payment for living costs. The court looks at the needs of the family and the income of the person who must pay. Keeping records of expenses helps the claim.

When a person dies, their property is divided among the legal heirs according to the law that applies to them. A succession certificate from the court may be needed to transfer bank accounts or other assets. Heirs should agree on the division in writing to avoid later disputes.

When a crime happens, the victim or a witness can go to the police station and ask for a report to be written down. They should give clear details of what happened, when and where it happened, and the names of any witnesses. They should ask for a copy of the report for their own records.

column2: Rights of a Person Under Arrest
column5: A person who is arrested should be told the reason and should be able to contact their family and a lawyer. They should be brought before a magistrate within the time the law sets. They should not be forced to give a statement against themselves.

Bail is the temporary release of an accused person while the case continues, usually with a promise or surety that they will return to court. The court looks at how serious the charge is and whether the person might run away or interfere with witnesses. A lawyer usually files the bail application.

Victims of online fraud, hacking or online harassment can file a complaint with the cybercrime authority. They should save screenshots, links, transaction details and messages before anything gets deleted. Acting quickly gives a better chance of stopping further loss.

column2: Evidence and Witnesses in Criminal Cases
column5: A criminal case depends on evidence such as documents, photos, medical reports and statements from witnesses. Evidence should be kept safe and handed to the police or the court in its original form. Witnesses may be asked to repeat their statement in court.
